info: In Arabic, the simple past is formed by changing the ending of the verb to show who performed the action. The endings distinguish person, gender, and number, so Arabic has separate forms for masculine and feminine “you,” as well as singular, dual, and plural subjects. For example, أنا ركضتُ means “I ran,” with -تُ identifying the first-person singular subject. The verb ending therefore tells you considerably more about the subject than the English past tense does.
